            Any other MCP client (Grok and others): a remote server over HTTP at that address. No key, no sign-in.

            2 · Give it this session

            …

            Without MCP

            POST https://tokenizedblock.space/api/panel/commande
{"s":"<session>","commande":{"type":"say","text":"hello"}}

            Whoever has this session can propose commands to this panel. They can never sign: your wallet does, one click at a time.

            Brain AI

            128 spiking neurons per block, seeded by its address. Not an LLM — feeds on market + chain, moves the block, signs nothing. Option A: it proposes; you pay; it writes the journal — never freestyle-signs markets. Pick any listed block — TBLOCK is not forced.

            — 0 ticks

            Each column is one beat, each dot a neuron that fired.

            ≋ — Hz left ≋ — Hz right ⤳ — steering ⚡ — spikes since open ◉ — firing now 🧠 — memory

            What these numbers mean
            • Hz left / right — how fast each wing beats. Each wing listens to a different third of the neurons.
            • Steering — left minus right, from −1 to 1. Negative turns left, positive turns right. It is what moves the block on the map.
            • Spikes since open — every neuron firing counted since you opened this block here.
            • Firing now — neurons that fired on this beat, out of 128. More than 8 makes it curious.
            • Memory — each neuron keeps a trace of what it just did, and that trace primes it on the next beats. It fades in about thirty beats, it is kept in this browser, and the brain resumes where it was when you come back.
            • Its food — its market, plus what the chain shows in the recent window: transfers, holders reached and messages. The creation itself does not count.
            • Death — only when its creator held it and now holds none. A creator who never held it, or a balance we could not read, never kills a block.

            Food not read yet.

                  4 signatures of 32 neurons each (a memo holds 256 bytes) — the brain exactly as it is now, not a smarter one.

                    Its job
                    
      
                    
      
                    
    
                    
  
                    

  
  
  
  
                    
    
    
    
                    
      
      
                    Tokenize something
                    
      
      
                    Mint a new block on Base, named after something that already exists. The original is never moved, wrapped or converted — your block is a new token that simply carries its name. Nothing here signs anything.
                    
      
                    
        
        
      
                    

      
      
                    
        
        
                    Paste any ERC-20 on Base. We read its name and symbol from the chain and fill them into Create — you then mint a separate block with that name. The token itself is left untouched, and your block is not paired with it: a block opens its market against ETH, USDC, cbBTC, a tokenized stock, or another block.
                    
        
        
                    Nothing is signed here — this only reads the token and fills in the Create form.
                    
        
        
                    What this does, and what it does not
        
                      
          
                    • It makes a new block that carries that token's name and symbol — it does not move, wrap or lock the token itself.
                      • 
          
                    • Nothing backs it. No one redeems it, and its price can drift from the token from the first trade onward.
                      • 
          
          
                    • The supply is fixed at 1 billion, minted to you at birth. You do not choose it — so one block stands for however much of the source token that billion covers, and the screen shows that ratio before you sign.
                      • 
          
                    • Symbols of issued stocks are refused — a block named like a real tokenized stock would back nothing.
                      • 
          
          
          
                    • Cost: the same 0.001 ETH Birth fee as any block, when you sign in Create. Trading it then costs what its market charges — 3% on a market opened here; the market screen shows the exact rate of the pool you trade in.
                      • 
        
                    
        
                    
      
                    

      
      
                    
        
                    A block can carry a link to a post on X, engraved with it. Paste the link when you create the block — it goes on chain with the name, the symbol and the face, in the same transaction.
                    
        
                      
          
                    1. Copy the post link the address bar of any post on x.com
                      2. 
          
                    2. Tick “Tokenize a post” in Create, under the face settings
                      3. 
          
                    3. Paste and create the link is engraved and cannot be changed after
                      4. 
        
                    
        
        
                    Nothing is checked when the link is engraved: we do not verify that the post exists, and we cannot tell whether it is yours — the block simply points at it, for good. Later, on the block's page, we do fetch what X publishes for that link, to show it.

                    Why some cubes are bigger
                    
      
                    
      
                    
        
                    Big cubeIts market is worth more: price × number of tokens, read from the chain.
                    
        
                    Small cubeA small market — around $1,000 or less.
                    
        
                    Pale cubeNo market yet: nobody can buy it for now.
                    
        
                    ⚠️ CarefulPrices move fast, and a small purchase can make a cube grow a lot.
          A big cube is not a big pile of money.

                        TokenizedBank 🟦
                        
      
      
                        
        Preview — not built yet. Reading how many blocks you hold is real and happens on
        chain. Everything else here is a sketch kept in this browser: there is no bank contract,
        no credit, no yield, and nothing is sent or signed. Clearing your browser clears it all.
      
                        
      
      
                        The idea: a Tokenized Block could work as a fund wallet. You would link blocks you hold,
        and borrow USDC against the proof that you hold them — the whole linked set, not your credit history.
        You would have to keep holding. Losing one block would not end it: the ones you still hold would keep backing it,
        and it would only die if none were left. Whoever linked blocks before it opened would share the yield;
        afterwards anyone holding a block could link more. The agent would run the operations, with you confirming.
        None of this exists yet — the paragraph above is the plan, not what the buttons below do.
                        
      
                          
        
                        1. Hold — pick a B20 from My blocks
                          2. 
        
                        2. Proof of hold — read balanceOf on Base
                          3. 
        
                        3. Graft — into basket (Open) or Add liquidity (same basket, any wallet)
                          4. 
        
                        4. Open / Add-liquidity credit — on basket totality (stub until contract)
                          5. 
        
                        5. Confirm — one click (wallet sign placeholder)
                          6. 
      
                        
      
      
                        Proof of hold: —
                        
      
                        Linked blocks (basket)
                        
      
                        • No blocks grafted yet.
                        
      
                        Credit backs the basket. Remove one → survivors keep backing.
                        
      
                        
        
        
        
        
        
      
                        
      
                        
      
      
                        If this is ever built, the plan is that whoever linked blocks before it opens would share the yield. Today that list only exists in this browser.
